120	A lion: if you tell him, "How about being a rabbit?"
121	"Act like
122	a rabbit." A lion is a lion, he won't be a rabbit. And if
123	we tell a rabbit, "Maybe be strong like a mighty lion,
124	like a lion, pounce on everyone, bite them," he's a rabbit.
125	Every animal has its own particular trait. A person
126	gathers within himself the traits of all the animals,
127	and he can choose how to direct them. The Mishnah
128	says: "Be bold as a leopard,
129	light as an eagle,
130	and mighty as a lion." What does all this mean? That you should be like the animals.
131	The meaning is to take the central trait. You
132	see that the lion has the trait of courage. You too
133	should be courageous. In the Shulchan Aruch it is written: "Strengthen yourself to rise
134	in the morning for the service of the Creator." He went to sleep late, after
135	his brother's wedding, at one at night, but he knows the time
136	of the Shema,
137	that it must not pass. He strengthens himself, washes his hands, before dawn, the Shema.
138	After that he can sleep a bit more, but he must not
139	miss the time of the Shema. He strengthens himself like a lion. It is
140	a Torah mitzvah to recite the Shema at its time.
141	"Bold." So the friends say to him, "You started walking around with
142	a kippah, you need to be
143	bold." The Mishnah ends there: "The bold-faced goes to Gehinnom, the shamefaced
144	to Gan Eden." But you told me to be bold, and now
145	you say the bold-faced goes to Gehinnom? The meaning depends
146	on what: in matters of holiness you are doing the right thing,
147	something good. You see all the friends pouncing on
148	one person, shaming him, humiliating him. You go out to defend him,
149	but you say, "If I go out to defend him, they'll shout
150	at me, they'll shame me too." Be bold as a leopard. You see
151	that here a person is being humiliated unjustly. Be
152	strong like a leopard. We all know how a leopard
153	looks when he wants to. What a look he has
154	in his eyes. Be firm like that: "Why are you
155	shaming him? What do you want from him? He's a good person."
156	But if a person is insolent toward his parents, toward those greater
157	than him, then that is already "the bold-faced goes to Gehinnom." That is,
158	the trait
159	of boldness you can take for the good or for the bad.
160	So here it says:
161	"light as an eagle." The eagle has wings, but you see
162	him, when he wants to rise, suddenly with such
163	lightness he flies upward. You too need
164	to be somewhat quick. Rise up, move,
165	be mighty
166	as a lion, "run
167	like a deer." The deer, what quickness he has to do the will of
168	your Father in Heaven. There is someone to help, a
169	mitzvah matter, a Torah class: be a runner like a deer, be
170	quick. So you see that all the traits found in animals,
171	a person has the choice. You can be like
172	this, you can be like a rabbit. Sometimes
173	people say, "That one is like a lion, and this one is like a snake."
174	Sometimes that is how they speak about people: "Be careful of him,
175	he's like a snake." What does it mean? Like a snake: you see
176	him calm, suddenly he bites you without you feeling it.
177	You don't know from which side. Why? He's cunning.
178	Be careful of him. People use these expressions
179	about human beings by comparison to animals. Because
180	man, our Sages say, is a small world. Everything
181	in the world can be in man.
182	And if that is not enough, note that also
183	the sounds: man is the only one who can produce all
184	the sounds
185	from within himself. Take for example a sheep. Tell it, "Say
186	the letter tzadik." Look, learn from the bird,
187	it knows how to chirp, to say the letter tzadik.
188	The sheep cannot say tzadik. It has mem, it has
189	heh, but it cannot express all the letters.
190	Every animal has certain letters
191	that it is able to pronounce in its own
192	sound. Man is the only one who can combine all
193	the letters, all the sounds, to resemble the Holy One,
194	blessed be He. And this obligates man greatly. You
195	resemble Elokim, you received powers, you resemble the whole
196	world. Use it
197	for good. On the other hand, the world is in fact parallel
198	to the human body. Therefore
199	our Sages say that if we examine the Tanakh, there are countries that the Torah
200	calls by the name of one of the organs of the
201	human body, because it teaches about the trait of that
202	nation of that
203	country. Eretz
204	Yisrael is considered the center of the world, Yerushalayim like
205	the heart. The Even HaShetiá, which is on the Temple
206	Mount, it is written that from it the world was founded. To this day,
207	on the Temple Mount, in their mosque, there is the Even HaShetiá,
208	which is visible, and they treat it as something
209	special. On the Even HaShetiá stood the Ark of the Covenant
210	in the Holy of
211	Holies. From it the world was founded, meaning it is
212	in fact the base, like a seed from which everything developed, the whole
213	globe, everything in the world. So this is the heart. What is
214	interesting is that our Sages revealed to us something the researchers do not
215	know, something connected to the world of
216	nature. Here, in the introduction to Kohelet, we brought many of the praises of
217	Shlomo HaMelech, and among them the words of the Ramban. We will read
218	his words in the introduction to the Torah. He writes as follows. He
219	speaks here about the wisdom of
220	Shlomo. His aim was not now to praise
221	Shlomo. He wanted,
222	the Ramban in the introduction to the Torah, to explain to us what Torah is,
223	what is hidden in the Torah. And he says that the whole
224	Torah, if you remove the spaces between
225	the words, "Bereshit" has a space, "bara" has a space,
226	remove all the
227	spaces, you get a giant table of
228	letters, where all the letters in the Torah, when in sequence, have
229	many ways of reading. You can read
230	it with divisions of words in different ways, skipping
231	letters, and you can get there all the secrets
232	of creation. That is, the Torah is in fact like
233	a code containing millions of letters, and this code
234	contains the program of all creation. Therefore
235	he says, everything that exists in reality, say every person
236	of those sitting here, all of us, you must
237	be encoded in the Torah, because if we were not in the Torah,
238	we would not be here either. It is like when you see in a building
